description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the modules-work battery (#1994: `~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/modwork/`, mw-07).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.  Narrowed with an instrumented copy of File/Find.pm (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/ffdbg/`, find2.pl: `_find_opt` is entered with 3 args, its top-item loop body never runs).
REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/localglob1.pl, find1.pl):
  sub f { my $w = shift; local *_ = \my $a; "args=" . scalar(@_) . " first=" . ($_[0] // "UNDEF") }   f("w", "x", "y")     perl args=2 first=x      PCL args=0 first=UNDEF
  sub h { local *_; scalar(@_) }  h(1, 2, 3)                                                           perl 0                   PCL 0        (a BARE `local *_` does clear it in perl too -- keep)
  sub k { local *_ = \my $t; $_ = "inner"; $_ }  with $_ = "outer" outside                              inner / outer restored on both   (the scalar half is right)
  use File::Find; find(sub { push @a, $_ }, $root);   perl: every entry     PCL: @a EMPTY, no error   (all four spellings in find1.pl, incl. no_chdir and finddepth)
perl's rule: `local *name = \$x` / `= \@x` / `= \%x` / `= sub {...}` / `= \&f` saves and replaces ONLY that slot; every other slot of the glob keeps its value (that is what makes the everyday test-mock idiom `local *Foo::bar = sub { ... };` leave `$Foo::bar` / `@Foo::bar` alone); `local *name = *other` and bare `local *name` localize the whole glob.  WHERE: the emission / runtime for `local` on a typeglob followed by a reference assignment (grep the `p-local` glob arm and `p-glob-assign`); probe all five reference kinds + the glob-to-glob form + `local *STDOUT` (whole glob -- unchanged) + `local *_ = \$x` inside a sub that then calls ANOTHER sub with `&inner;` (shares @_).
ACCEPTANCE: localglob1.pl, find1.pl == perl; `modwork/mw-07-File-Path-Find.pl` == perl; battery2's b2-28 once #2007 is in.  BAR: emission or `cl/` => corpus-diff (grep the corpus for `local \*`: list the sites), full sweep, companion op/local.t op/gv.t legs + lib/File/Find t/ if in the population, CPAN board by ROWS (File::Find is everywhere -- expect UPWARD movers), guard rows in an existing local/glob Pl/t file, INVERSE-verified.


=== DONE (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2080: `local *name = REF` localizes ONLY the slot the reference names".

ONE READING (rule 11): `%p-glob-rhs-slot-kind` is the classification `%p-glob-assign-slots` already
made to decide WHERE to store, lifted out so `local` can ask it BEFORE the assignment;
`%p-glob-clear` takes that answer as a KIND argument, and all three localizers consult it.
`p-local-glob` gained the RHS in the same argument slot `p-local-glob-if` and `p-local-glob-dynamic`
already had it in (`:none` for the assignment-less spelling), so the codegen's wrapping `let` plus a
separate `p-glob-assign` first body form is gone: the macro is what knows the RHS must be evaluated
before the slots are touched.  Bare `local *name` and `local *name = *other` still take the WHOLE
glob, which is perl.

A SECOND BUG FELL OUT OF THE SAME READ (rule 12): `%p-glob-clear` unbound the CODE slot's function
but left its `*p-declared-subs*` entry, so inside a bare `local *X` the guard `defined &X` was TRUE
with nothing to call -- it killed the guard row's own program.  Save and restore had always carried
that entry; only the clear half was missing.

MEASURED: corpus-diff 8 of 111 files, every diff the `p-local-glob` spelling (`:none` added, or the
wrapping let folded in) plus the paren depth that follows; the eight keep their blessed row counts.
PROBES vs perl 5.40.3: localglob1, localglob3 (13 rows over all five reference forms plus the glob
and bare spellings), find1 (four File::Find spellings, incl. no_chdir and finddepth) and
modwork/mw-07-File-Path-Find.pl are now identical; every one was wrong on the base.
NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 7.2.
GUARD: Pl/t/local-glob-slot-01.t, 5 rows, all 5 failing on a 5ce155cb extraction.
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday: File::Find finds NOTHING): `local *_ = \my $a;` clears the sub's `@_` -- perl's `local *GLOB = REF` localizes ONLY the slot the reference names (here the SCALAR), PCL localizes the WHOLE glob; core File::Find's `_find_opt` starts with exactly that line and then loops `foreach my $TOP (@_)`, so `find(sub {...}, $dir)` calls `wanted` ZERO times, silently
